Abdul Rehman

Five years of NO₂ over Lahore, seen from space and from the ground

Environmental Sciences graduate (UET Lahore) working with GIS, remote sensing and air quality data. This page shows my final year thesis: ten zones of Lahore, Sentinel-5P satellite data and Punjab EPA monitors, 2021 to 2025.

Team project with Amna Amin and Awais Javaid. Supervisor: Dr. Irfan Jalees, Institute of Environmental Engineering and Research, UET Lahore. Click any figure to enlarge it.

Study area and data

I split central Lahore into ten grid zones (“slices”) and compared two data sources: daily satellite NO₂ from Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI, processed in Google Earth Engine, and ground readings from Punjab EPA monitoring stations. Maps were made in QGIS and statistics in Excel and Minitab (ANOVA, Pearson correlation, RMSE and MAE).

How NO₂ changes through the year

Winter is the highest season in every zone, and summer is the lowest. Satellite NO₂ is highest in January and December and lowest in July and August.

Satellite and ground data do not agree closely

The satellite citywide mean fell after 2022, while the EPA ground mean rose every year from 2021 to 2025. The two sources measure different things (a column through the atmosphere from space, and air at street level), and daily agreement between them was weak (r = 0.011). I treat this as a finding about validation, not a flaw to hide.

Pollution episodes in the ground record

The strongest sustained episodes fall in November and December, when smog builds up in Lahore.

What the thesis shows

  • NO₂ is consistently highest in Mughalpura, Samanabad and Model Town, and lowest in Shahdara and Iqbal Town.
  • Winter is the highest season and summer the lowest, with a repeated winter rise each year.
  • Satellite NO₂ fell after 2022 while ground readings rose, so satellite data alone should not be used to judge ground-level air quality without validation.
